topic.title: Biological Foundation Models and Functional Representation
topic.area: Molecular, Biological, and Quantum Machine Learning
topic.overview: Biological foundation models learn reusable representations from sequences or other molecular data, with applications to fitness prediction, functional interpretation, and transfer between modalities. This topic studies architecture, scaling, retrieval, and the relationship between learned features and biological meaning. Predictive patterns must be distinguished from experimentally established mechanisms.
topic.whyItMatters: Large biological datasets offer broad coverage, but performance can depend on which organisms, molecules, and tasks resemble training examples. Scaling results and representation analyses help identify useful design choices; they do not by themselves establish therapeutic value or reliable behavior on unfamiliar biological interventions.
topic.evolution: A 1993 study learns alternative protein secondary-structure classes that are more predictable from sequence. Later representatives connect expression data, protein fitness, and cross-modal transfer. Recent work interprets protein-model features and studies RNA transfer; a 2026 metagenomic analysis compares transformer, state-space, and convolutional architectures and derives empirical scaling relationships within its training regime.
openQuestions: Which learned biological features correspond to mechanisms that survive experimental intervention?
How can transfer evaluations expose failures on distant species or underrepresented molecular families?

papers.tldr: SP-Mind coordinates spatial proteomics tools into natural-language-driven workflows and outperforms evaluated open-source biomedical agents.

papers.title: SpaEF: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomics Data Element-Wise Denoising Framework Powered by Large Models
papers.tldr: SpaEF uses pretrained large models to build spot and gene graphs, then fuses them to improve spatial transcriptomics denoising.

papers.title: SPATIA: Multimodal Generation and Prediction of Spatial Cell Phenotypes
papers.tldr: SPATIA integrates cell images, gene expression, and spatial context to improve phenotype generation and prediction across multiple tissue-analysis tasks.

papers.title: STRIDE: Post-Training LLMs to Reason and Refine Bio-Sequences via Edit Trajectories
papers.tldr: STRIDE trains language models to refine biological sequences through executable edit trajectories aligned with task rewards.

papers.title: TadA-Bench: A Million-Variant Benchmark for Future-Round Discovery Toward Agentic Protein Engineering
papers.tldr: TadA-Bench preserves experimental chronology to reveal how much harder future protein-variant discovery is than random-split prediction.

papers.title: Towards A Generative Protein Evolution Machine with DPLM-Evo
papers.tldr: DPLM-Evo learns explicit protein substitutions, insertions, and deletions to improve sequence modeling and enable variable-length generation and editing.

papers.title: Towards Universal Gene Regulatory Network Inference: Unlocking Generalizable Regulatory Knowledge in Single-cell Foundation Models
papers.tldr: Two extraction methods turn implicit knowledge in single-cell foundation models into regulatory features that generalize to unseen genes and datasets.

papers.title: Transitive Representation Learning Enhances Histopathology Annotation
papers.tldr: SpatialWhisperer uses gene expression to connect tissue images with textual cell labels, improving zero-shot histopathology annotation.

papers.title: Tree-Structured Orthonormal Decomposition of the Aitchison Simplex
papers.tldr: PolyILR builds complete, tree-aligned coordinates for compositional data while preserving Aitchison geometry and supporting interpretable multiscale analysis.

papers.title: Understanding Transfer Learning of RNA Foundation Models on Downstream Tasks
papers.tldr: RNA pretraining primarily helps optimization when objectives align, while frozen features are not universally transferable across downstream tasks.
